claims.text: Post-fabrication deep cryogenic treatment will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-fabrication deep cryogenic treatment will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
As-deposited laser-additively-manufactured HEA components exhibit residual stress, microstructural defects, and minor dimensional distortions.
Deep cryogenic treatment can be applied as a post-processing method after laser melting deposition of a BCC Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEA.
Extended cryogenic immersion promotes microstructural transformation.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in the additively manufactured HEA.
The induced phase transition forms HCP precipitates near grain boundaries.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases grain-boundary density by utilizing residual stress.
Deep cryogenic treatment relieves residual stresses accumulated during rapid solidification.
Deep cryogenic treatment promotes lattice distortion.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the microstructure.
Residual-stress relief, lattice distortion, phase transformation, and microstructural refinement collectively reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment will reduce the number and size of fabrication-induced defects relative to the untreated as-deposited baseline.
Deep cryogenic treatment will increase tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated as-deposited baseline.
Mechanical-property improvements on the order of approximately 11–25% have been reported in a similar additively manufactured HEA system.
The expected benefit applies to LMD-processed BCC Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr-type HEAs.
The direct correlation between deep cryogenic treatment and improved dimensional precision remains unquantified.
The quantitative reduction in fabrication-induced defects after deep cryogenic treatment remains unquantified.
